title: Yashasvi Jaiswal Plays 30th Test at 30th Different Venue, Closes in on Manjrekar Record
excerpt: The 24-year-old opener has never played at the same Test ground twice since his 2023 debut, placing him just three behind Sanjay Manjrekar's all-time Indian record of 33 consecutive Tests at different venues.
body:
• Yashasvi Jaiswal has now played 30 Test matches at 30 different venues, extending an extraordinary record that only two Indians — Sanjay Manjrekar (33) and Sachin Tendulkar (32) — have surpassed.
  • The milestone came in the first Test against Sri Lanka, where Jaiswal scored 32 off 37 balls before being run out as India batted first after winning the toss.
  • Since his debut against the West Indies at Roseau in July 2023, the 24-year-old left-hander has never played at the same Test ground twice.
  • Jaiswal has amassed over 2,500 runs in his Test career at an average near 49, with seven centuries and 13 half-centuries.

A Record Three Years in the Making

When Yashasvi Jaiswal walked out to bat in the first Test against Sri Lanka on August 14, he added another line to one of cricket's most unusual records. The match marked his 30th Test appearance — and his 30th at a different venue.

https://x.com/Cricadium/status/2088489295917240415

Since making his debut against the West Indies at Windsor Park in Roseau in July 2023, the left-handed opener has never returned to the same Test ground. Every match has been played on fresh turf, a streak that now places him just three behind Sanjay Manjrekar's all-time Indian record of 33 consecutive Tests at different venues, according to SportsCafe.

"All of the Test matches Jaiswal has played have been at different venues."

— SportsCafe, noting the rare record in November 2025

Following Tendulkar's Footsteps

The record puts Jaiswal in elite company. Only two Indians have managed longer streaks: Manjrekar, who played 33 of his 37 career Tests at different grounds between 1987 and 1996, and Sachin Tendulkar, who holds the second spot with 32. Jaiswal, at 24, has time and India's packed touring schedule on his side.

The streak has been fueled by India's relentless Test calendar. Jaiswal's career has taken him from the Caribbean to South Africa, across five English venues during the 2025 Anderson-Tendulkar Trophy, through Australia during the Border-Gavaskar Trophy, and to New Chandigarh for the Afghanistan Test in June 2026. The Sri Lanka tour now adds another country to his logbook.

More Than a Curiosity

The venue record is a statistical quirk, but it reflects something more substantive: Jaiswal's consistent selection across conditions. In 54 innings through 29 Tests before this match, he had scored 2,535 runs at an average of 48.75, according to Sportskeeda. His seven centuries include two double-hundreds against England in the 2024 home series — 206 at Visakhapatnam and an unbeaten 200 at Rajkot — and a match-defining 161 at Perth during the Border-Gavaskar Trophy.

His debut knock of 171 against the West Indies at Roseau remains one of the most impressive first appearances in Indian Test history. At 21 years and 196 days, Jaiswal became the fifth-youngest batter to register a 150-plus score on Test debut, joining a list that includes Javed Miandad and Doug Walters.

A Steady Start in Sri Lanka

In the ongoing first Test, Jaiswal scored 32 off 37 balls with five fours before being run out by Prabath Jayasuriya. India, batting first after captain Shubman Gill won the toss, were 152 for 1 at the time of the dismissal, with KL Rahul (52 not out) and Devdutt Padikkal (67 not out) building a solid partnership.

The venue tally will continue to grow only if India's schedule keeps sending Jaiswal to new grounds. With the second Test in the series still to come, and future tours on the horizon, the left-hander could have Manjrekar's record in his sights before the year is out.

What's Next

For Jaiswal, the immediate focus remains on the Sri Lanka series, a crucial fixture in India's World Test Championship campaign. Whether the venue record is broken will depend on scheduling quirks as much as performance — but if his first 30 Tests are any indication, Jaiswal will be making his mark wherever he plays.
